chapter: Coming to New Orleans and building the band
title: Band uniforms, deaths of members and forming his own band
summary: He kept the blue uniforms; members died and he started his own band with Edmund Washington, Sammy and others; a question about the banjoist Fan.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: No, they ain't got nothing. I'm the only one got them pictures. So, alright. Like, you take like the uniforms. We used to wear a uniform, we had a jacket, a blue jacket, with a dark lapel, you know what I mean? And, blue pants with stripes. And, you know what I mean? None of them fellas don't have the jacket and the pants. I'm still got them. You stayed here? And that been years ago. I even got them white pants we used to wear. Even got that. See? You know what? Sometimes boys see me, we say, man, what? See, they ain't them same pants. I said that. He said, man, I ain't long wear that. The blue shirt I would, with your head, you know? So, alright. So, well I tell you what happened. Then, the bass player, he died. The drum player, Johnny Thomas, he died. Teep Ruchon, he died. That was two fellas of the band. So, we got another boy, Alvin Clemons, we got him to play. Nice drummer, had good instruments. Good instruments, that boy, and he was a nice drummer, you know what I mean? So, well poor boy, he died too. See? So, after he died, well that made us got, I got, see, well I got away from that band. This band, the first band, the band, you know what I mean? I got away from them fellas, you see? I organized my own band then, you see? That was, that was, I got Edmund Washington, and Sammy, and uh, who was playing bass with us? Bikes? And uh, who else? Oh yeah. I even had this fella boy, Henry Harden, playing saxophone with us too. I remember we had another boy playing saxophone with us, Alito saxophone, John Smith. He died. That was three, three members we lost in our band. Have any piano? Yeah we had piano, Joe James, the same piano player. What about fan? You see, we didn't. Did fan bourgeois ever play with you? Fan? Yeah.
Where you live in? He lives out on, oh near Roman Street.

Well I'll tell you, I'll tell you, probably Mr. Billy. Fan? Yeah. He plays banjo too. Well I'll tell you, probably, probably play with him, cause you know we used to hire, we used to hire plenty of fellas like that. Sometime like a fella, you know what I mean, we'd need a fella, well we'd hire him, you know, something like that.
